outcome: Abnormal CUS findings (intraventricular hemorrhage, features of meningitis, hydrocephalus, prominent lateral and third ventricles, intracerebral hemorrhage, features of ventriculitis)
cohort: The study included inborn neonates with sepsis and inborn preterm neonates without sepsis, all admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) at Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujib Medical University (BSMMU).
finding: Proven sepsis was significantly associated with abnormal cranial ultrasound (CUS) findings, with 37.5% of septic neonates showing such abnormalities.
birth_weight: Mean 1985.2+/-684.132 gm for septic neonates with abnormal CUS findings
gest_age: Mean 34.57+/-3.043 weeks for septic neonates with abnormal CUS findings
